_schema_notes.purpose: Reference dataset of LLM SDK call-site shapes for JavaScript/TypeScript source, the companion to llm_api_functions.json (which covers Rust/MIR). Used by find_llm_calls_js to scan frontend code that a Rust-only tool like RUPTA can never see, e.g. the webview/JS side of a Tauri app.
_schema_notes.usage: find_llm_calls_js walks a directory of .js/.jsx/.ts/.tsx/.mjs/.cjs files. For each entry, it looks for the literal text `<pattern>(` on a line. If any of the entry's `packages` was also seen imported (via import/require/dynamic import) in the same file, match_strategy is "call+import"; otherwise "call-only". Both are reported — call-only is not discarded, since bundled/minified output often strips or rewrites import statements while leaving property-access chains intact.
_schema_notes.verification_caveat: Unlike llm_api_functions.json's Rust entries (checked against docs.rs/context7), these signatures come from general knowledge of each SDK's public API shape and have not been independently re-verified against current published docs. JS SDKs iterate faster than the Rust crates this pipeline was originally built for — spot-check patterns against the target's actual installed SDK version (package.json) before trusting a `call-only` match strongly.
_schema_notes.raw_http_note: The raw-http-fetch entry has no call patterns of its own; find_llm_calls_js treats any fetch()/axios()/XMLHttpRequest/http(s).request() call as a candidate and only reports it when a known LLM REST path suffix (shared PROVIDER_PATH_HINTS table, same one llm_api_finder.rs uses) is found in a string literal on a nearby line. This mirrors the Rust tool's raw-http-reqwest + provider_hint pairing, but for JS the hint is required by default (not just attached) because fetch()/axios() are far too common in ordinary frontend code to report unconditionally — see --all-http-calls in find_llm_calls_js to disable the gate.

calls.kind: legacy completion (also matches Anthropic's legacy shape)
token counting (not a generation call, but SDK-confirming)
chat send (also matches unrelated messaging UIs without --require-import)
chat send (useChat()/Chat hook from @ai-sdk/react — same method name as google-genai's chat session send, disambiguate via import)
runnable invoke (very generic — langchain Runnables, chains, and tools all share this method name)
